title: UNIVERSAL VENTILATED FAÇADE SYSTEM
subtitle: VENTILATED FAÇADE CLADDING WITH PIR INSULATION
cardDescription: Flexible ventilated façade construction with PIR insulation and a choice of durable exterior finishes.
metaTitle: Universal Ventilated Façade System | EcoViva Mallorca
metaDescription: Technical guidance for a universal ventilated façade with PIR insulation, drained cavity, supporting substructure and durable cladding options in Mallorca.
heroAlt: Universal ventilated façade build-up with five numbered callouts identifying the masonry wall, PIR insulation, substructure, ventilated cavity and exterior cladding.
cleanHeroAlt: Clean universal ventilated façade build-up with masonry wall, PIR insulation, battens and grey exterior panels.
overview: The universal ventilated façade combines continuous PIR insulation, a supporting substructure, a drained cavity and durable exterior cladding. The cavity promotes airflow and drainage while helping protect the wall. The system supports broad architectural choice in colour, format, texture and material.
overviewNote: Final design must verify the substrate, building height, wind and fire requirements, ventilation openings, fixings, panel format and project conditions.
why: One point of contact from concept to completion
layers: Prepared masonry or structural wall supporting the façade system.
Continuous rigid insulation improving the external thermal envelope.
Rails transfer façade loads and establish the required cavity depth.
Open drainage and airflow space behind the exterior finish.
Durable outer finish defining the architectural appearance.
principles: Install PIR continuously outside the wall to limit thermal bridging.
Maintain a continuous cavity for upward airflow and safe drainage.
Select material, spacing and anchors for the cladding, wind and substrate.
Protect base and top openings while maintaining sufficient free area.
Coordinate fixings, joints and support spacing with the selected system.
Verify cavity barriers, fixing resistance and wind-load performance.
componentsTitle: EXAMPLES OF COMPONENTS USED IN THE SYSTEM
componentsIntro: Components are selected for the façade material, panel format, building height, exposure and project requirements.
components: Protects cavity openings while preserving airflow.
Supports clean and controlled panel joints.
materialsIntro: Six durable façade finishes illustrate the architectural flexibility of the ventilated system.
materials: Stone-wool façade panels combining design flexibility, durability and low maintenance.
Durable boards with a refined linear appearance and strong weather resistance.
Authentic, durable and non-combustible slate with distinctive overlapping patterns.
Durable laminate panels available in varied colours, textures and finishes.
Lightweight, recyclable cladding with precise joints and low maintenance.
Large-format tiles offering durable, stain-resistant and weather-resistant finishes.
benefits: Suitable for renovation and new construction
appearance: Appearance depends on material, finish and exposure. Manufactured panels may remain uniform, while natural slate varies in tone and texture. Confirm colour stability, cleaning, joints and weathering for the selected product.
requirements: Verify the wall and design anchors, rails and fixing centres for project wind loads. Maintain a continuous drained cavity with protected base and top openings. Select compatible substructure, panels and fixings for the fire strategy, coastal exposure and movement requirements. Coordinate openings, corners, roof, parapet and plinth interfaces; verify cavity barriers, drainage and contact-corrosion risks. Final design and execution must comply with the CTE, applicable product documentation and project requirements.
